title: Resilience Patterns: Circuit Breakers, Retries with Jitter & Rate Limiting
subtopicTitle: Resilience Patterns: Circuit Breakers, Retries with Jitter & Rate Limiting
problemStatement:
Preventing cascading system failures using the Circuit Breaker pattern, exponential backoff with jitter, and token bucket rate limiting.

**Architectural Importance**:
Without circuit breakers, one struggling third-party API or downstream database will exhaust all thread connections and crash your entire server fleet.
interviewTrap: Retrying failed requests immediately without exponential backoff or jitter, inadvertently launching a self-inflicted DDoS attack on your own database.

detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals:
## ⚡ System Resilience & Circuit Breakers

### The Circuit Breaker State Machine
```
          [ CLOSED ] (Normal operations)
              │
              │ (Failure rate > 50%)
              ▼
           [ OPEN ] (Fails fast immediately, 0 calls to backend)
              │
              │ (Cooldown timeout e.g. 30s elapsed)
              ▼
        [ HALF-OPEN ] (Sends 3 trial requests)
        ├── If Successful ──> Back to [ CLOSED ]
        └── If Failed ──────> Back to [ OPEN ]
```

### Retries with Exponential Backoff and Jitter
When a network call fails, retry using:
```javascript
const delay = Math.min(maxDelay, baseDelay * Math.pow(2, attempt)) + Math.random() * 100;
```
The `+ Math.random() * 100` is **jitter**. Without jitter, 5,000 requests that failed at the exact same moment will all retry at the exact same millisecond, crushing the recovering service!
